papers.title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability
papers.abstract: The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form. These sets are computed from the image alone, so calibrating from many junctions is a convex feasibility problem. Almost every junction bounds the focal length from below; we characterize when one also bounds it from above, and when many junctions determine it exactly. For a known vertex, the bounds can be certified against any bounded error in the measured edge directions.

papers.title: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $\pi$. We show that $\pi^2 = p\,\alpha_*$ for a unique automorphism $\alpha$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius. For $p \ge 7$ this gives the list of Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points: eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on $p$, and its number 15, 3, 3, 7, 1, 1, 3 or 1 of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational $(2,2)$-kernels; when all Weierstrass points are rational, the 2-Tate pairing on $J[2]$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$. We then prove closed formulas, in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders and of $\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt p)}(-1)$, for the mass of the curves of each type and for the mass of the rational kernels whose quotient is a product of elliptic curves. For $\pi^2 = \pm p$ the total masses are due to Ibukiyama and to Xue and Yu; our proofs use the 2-adic Tate modules, the symmetry of the Richelot correspondence and Eichler's mass formula, and, for the other curves, modules over orders of a quartic CM field. The kernels are counted through gluings of supersingular elliptic curves. As a consequence, the proportion of rational kernels with decomposed quotient is of order $p^{-1/2}(1+L(1,\chi))$, where $\chi$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$. All formulas agree with an exact enumeration for the 37 primes $7 \le p \le 173$. Finally we describe the graph of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational Richelot isogenies, which is far from connected in the range computed, and discuss what these results say about its use in isogeny-based cryptography.

papers.title: Cohomology Rings of Fiber Products of Lefschetz Fibrations
papers.abstract: We prove a Lefschetz-type theorem for the cohomology rings of fiber products of two Lefschetz fibrations with disjoint critical loci. As an application, we compute the Hodge numbers of several examples of higher-dimensional Schoen's Calabi-Yau manifolds.

papers.title: Convergence of the big J-function of a GKM manifold
papers.abstract: The genus-$0$ equivariant Gromov--Witten (GW) invariants of a GKM manifold can be computed recursively by a recursion discovered by Brown and studied further by Coates--Corti--Iritani--Tseng. In this paper, we prove a slightly modified version of this result by realizing the J-function as a solution to a fixed-point problem. As an application, we prove that both the equivariant and the non-equivariant quantum cohomologies of a GKM manifold are convergent. We also show that the equivariant central charges have no poles in the spectral parameter, compute their monodromy and their asymptotics at $z=0$, and formulate an equivariant mirror symmetry conjecture for GKM manifolds.

papers.title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
papers.abstract: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$. It controls, in a range of degrees, the restriction of natural transformations $\mathrm{id}\to F$ to the orthogonal complement of the collection, and it is computed from the collection by a finite complex. For collections of line bundles on surfaces whose Hom divisors have nonnegative canonical degree, the tensor product with a skyscraper sheaf has height exactly two, and the projections of skyscraper sheaves form a two-dimensional family of point-like objects in the orthogonal complement. We apply these tools to Orlov's rationality conjecture. A smooth projective complex surface is rational if its derived category has a full exceptional collection in which all members except possibly one are line bundles, or one that consists of at most three completely orthogonal blocks of arbitrary objects; we also obtain rationality in several cases with four blocks or with a hereditary component. If $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of the form $(M_i\boxtimes\mathcal O(a_i))$, then the $M_i$ with relative degrees of a fixed parity form a full exceptional collection on $S$; consequently $S$ is rational whenever $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. Finally, we show that the general case of the conjecture for surfaces is equivalent to the surjectivity and injectivity of two maps in Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
papers.abstract: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
papers.abstract: We study nef line bundles on polarized fibrations $(X/C,\bar{H})$, with a fixed nef metrized ample polarization satisfying $H^d=1$, where $d=\dim X$. We prove a quantitative arithmetic height inequality under relative metric positivity, allowing singular arithmetic models and relatively nef adelic bundles. The height deficit defines a local energy. For nef, relatively ample line bundles over finitely generated fields, this energy is bounded below for almost every complex or nonarchimedean local-field realization of fixed polarized global model data, outside one null set common to the entire relative metric class. The results include big non-semiample examples. For ample $L$ and smooth positively curved $\bar{H}$, the complex critical equation is the Calabi--Yau equation; at zero volume, projective bundles recover Donaldson's functional. We also study critical metrics and conjectural canonical heights defined by energy envelopes.

papers.title: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties
papers.abstract: We give a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties. We show that the determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals, thereby proving a conjecture of Alexandr-Mont\'ufar. The set-theoretic proof uses a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.

papers.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories
papers.abstract: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.

papers.title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

papers.title: On the slope stability of vector bundles on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the variation problem of slope stability of $T$-linearized sheaves on a compact Sasakian manifold, or more generally, on an affine variety with a good $T$-action. In particular, we establish the wall-and-chamber structure for the slope stability of $T$-linearized torsion-free sheaves.

papers.title: Note on parallel transport of IHS manifolds of Kummer type
papers.abstract: We give a characterization of parallel transport operators for irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of Kummer type.

papers.title: A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons. The main step towards deriving the semialgebraic description is the observation that we need to consider only finitely many ellipses that go through some of the vertices of the inner polygon and are tangent to some of the edges of the outer polygon. Although the description is not completely quantifier-free, for a general matrix, the quantified variables satisfy a system of polynomial equations that has at most four solutions corresponding to reduced conics.

papers.title: Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops
papers.abstract: We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.

papers.title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
papers.abstract: We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures. Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number

papers.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

papers.title: A Cohen--Macaulay Analogue of the Brodmann--Rotthaus Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove a Cohen--Macaulay analogue of the theorem of Brodmann and Rotthaus on the lifting of quasi-excellence. More precisely, let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I$ be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. We show that if $A/I$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-Q0 and $A$ is a $\mathsf{CM}$\textnormal{-G-}ring, then $A$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-quasi-excellent. Our proof follows the strategy of Kurano and Shimomoto and makes essential use of \v{C}esnavi\v{c}ius' Macaulayfication theorem.

papers.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
papers.abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. B\'erczi and Feh\'er conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one
papers.abstract: We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $\chi=\chi(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance. We prove that its nonvanishing condition holds whenever $\sum_i n_i\le2\chi+4$, where $I_{n_i}$ are the reducible fibers; hence every such surface is a Mori dream surface. Independently of this condition, we exclude ample generator degrees throughout the stated cone range. We also determine the section--fiber subring and give minimal complete-intersection presentations when all $s$ reducible fibers have type $I_2$ and $s\le2\chi+1$, including the endpoint beyond that cone range.

papers.title: Quasimonomial Monge--Amp\`ere equations for big classes
papers.abstract: Let X be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We describe an alternative approach to a differentiability result of volumes of norms defined by finitely many quasimonomial valuations. As a consequence, we prove the non-Archimedean Calabi--Yau theorem for quasimonomial measures on $X$ with respect to big classes, in the trivially valued case. We also obtain continuity of solutions as numerical classes vary in the big cone. This extends previous results of Boucksom--Jonsson and Dervan--Reboulet, and gives the first uniqueness results in the big case. Our approach relies on convex geometry and Okounkov bodies, without involving non-Archimedean pluripotential theory or test configurations.

papers.title: Combinatorial Bloch-Gieseker inequalities on toric surfaces
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial proof of the Bloch-Gieseker inequalities in the special case of ample toric vector bundles on toric surfaces via a new rearrangement inequality for planar curves. Using this we establish the Hodge package for combinatorial analogues of cohomology rings of ample projective bundles over toric surfaces which don't appear to arise from matroidal constructions.

papers.title: Singularities of ideals with minimal tangent space dimension in the Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold
papers.abstract: We classify all singular monomial ideals in the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points on $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose tangent spaces have the minimal dimension $3d+6$. There are two families called the opera houses and rotating staircases, and we give their combinatorial and algebraic descriptions. All the opera houses are in one linkage class, and their singularities are smoothly equivalent to the vertex of a cone over the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,6) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{14}$ in its Pl\"ucker embedding. The rotating staircases split into many linkage classes and we give some examples.

papers.title: On automorphisms of symplectic varieties acting trivially on the second cohomology group
papers.abstract: We prove that the group of automorphisms acting trivially on the torsion-free part of the integral second cohomology on a primitive symplectic variety is a locally trivial deformation invariant. We exhibit some examples of this invariant.

papers.title: Slope stability for normal varieties
papers.abstract: In this expository paper, we review the theory of slope stability of torsion-free sheaves with respect to nef curve classes and extend it to normal varieties.

papers.title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
papers.abstract: Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincar\'e polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$. Let $n\geq4$ and $W=S_n$ or $W(B_n)$. For $w\in W$ whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ satisfies $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=2$, we prove the sharp bound $[q^k]D_w(q)\leq[q^{k-1}]P_{w_0}(q)$ for $1\leq k<\ell(w)/2$. For every $n\geq3$ and $1\leq h\leq2n-4$, we construct an element $b=b_h^n\in W(B_n)$ with $P_{\mathrm{id},b}(q)=1+q^h$, and determine the asymmetry polynomial $D_b(q)$ and all Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,b}(q)$ for $x\leq b$.

papers.title: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
papers.abstract: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

papers.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
papers.abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $\lambda$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $\Delta^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.

papers.title: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
papers.abstract: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

papers.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces. As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

papers.title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
papers.abstract: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension.
